name: Mahali
slug: Mahali is an elder god who serves as the party's chef at their stronghold, welcoming them back with elaborate meals.
description: Mahali is an elder god who serves as the party’s chef. He is associated with the party’s stronghold and is known for welcoming the party back and preparing elaborate meals for them.

log.summary: Mahali followed Ben through the doorway into the traveling tavern and invited the party to return to the stronghold. He described a meal awaiting them there, featuring lamb soufflés, cabbage stew, and a choice of cherry or lemon curd.
notes: Follows Ben through the doorway into the traveling tavern.
Invites the party to return to the stronghold and describes a meal of lamb souffles, cabbage stew, and cherry or lemon curd.

log.summary: Mahali is unexpectedly encountered in his kitchen when Gerk opens a doorway into the stronghold. Initially confused, Mahali recognizes the resulting reality distortion as highly unnatural and pulls Gerk through the doorway when he is left hanging outside as the ship moves away. He learns that Gerk can now open doors to other places and, before the dangerous doorway is closed, provides the party with leftover breakfast rolls, preserves, and freshly churned butter. After Sylan raises concerns about the reality distortion, Mahali agrees to evacuate the stronghold’s residents and guards to the tavern as a precaution.

log.summary: Mahali was asked, through the guards, to prepare food for Glimmen ahead of Walker’s expected arrival by dragon. Sylan noted that an earlier doorway into the kitchen could have cut Mahali; the DM said that opening was a critical success. Mahali was not present for the forest practice.

log.summary: Mahali, also referred to as Moradin, calls himself a 'small deity' whose domain of hearth, home, and craftsmanship shifts with his current followers. Asked by Walker whether he became a god or was born one, he explained he became one unintentionally as belief in him grew, then claimed his domain. He described the Weave and ley lines, saying deities form from the Weave plus belief and are made tangible by mass belief; killing a god requires destroying both body and followers over many lifetimes. He calls the need for true believers a loophole of the universe, does not fight over the dead like other gods, and implied he hides his godhood to avoid hangers-on. He has been teaching Ponchi to cook and threw a thumb-sized gem found in one of Ponchi's buns out the window. He brewed lavender tea and cooked dinner, turning a tough pork flank into stew, with Walker chopping vegetables and Gerk mashing raw potatoes, which he plans to turn into breakfast hash. He bantered with Gerk about soul food and mildly hallucinogenic birch-leaf tea, served apple-pear-cinnamon summer cider, stew, and desserts, and advised contacting the helm's spirit late at night after dinner, wanting to watch.
